# Preface {.unnumbered}

<div style="display:flex">
<div style="flex:70%;margin-right:1em;">

This tutorial focuses on learning Git exclusively using terminal commands. The target audience is people with no prior experience with Git, version controls systems, or use of command-line interfaces. The aim of the tutorial is to learn how to use Git, but also to understand how Git works, at least on some superficial level, so that you don't end up in the situtation depicted in the webcomic.

The tutorial is structured in two parts. Part I is an introduction to Git, and goes through all the basic commands while giving some insights into what Git is and how it works along the way. Part II includes stand-alone chapters on more advanced topics. These chapters are not essential to learning how to use Git, and can be read to the extent they are relevant and of interest. Finally, the tutorial includes appendices on miscellaneous topics.

## Prerequisites

This tutorial assumes you are using Git version 2.51.0 or newer. If you are using an older version of Git, some of the `git config` commands in @sec-configuration-of-git might not work, and there might be other minor unknown issues as well.

This tutorial also assumes you are on a Windows machine and have "Git for Windows" installed. See @sec-git-for-windows for more details. Since we will be running Git exclusively from the command line using Git BASH, a BASH emulator, macOS and Linux users should also be able to follow along with only few modifications.

Finally, if you want to follow along in @sec-github, you will need to create a GitHub account and authenticate with it, using the GitHub CLI, which you also need to install. See @sec-github-setup for more details.
